title: THE BETA MEAN-vs-PROFILE CLOSURE -- recompute the window mean from the committed per-bin profile (log-uniform over [2,5] R500), re-test the 0.5 rule AT the envelope bin only, and resolve deepseek_moa CONTRADICTIONS #2

upstream.G203: projected-Jeans window mean beta_win(2-5 R500) = 0.434 +- 0.015 (10,145 HeCS members, 58 clusters)
upstream.G206: MAMPOSSt-class 2D likelihood beta_win(2-5 R500) = 0.495 +- 0.054; COMBINED 0.438 +- 0.014 excludes 0.5 at -4.4 sigma
upstream.G209: per-bin profile: 2-3 R500 = 0.305/0.256 (E1/E2); 3-5 R500 = 0.560/0.545 (E1/E2) -- the envelope reaching the 0.5 class

convention.kind: log-uniform integral over [2,5] R500: [b23 ln(3/2) + b35 ln(5/3)] / ln(5/2)
convention.proof: each committed window mean reproduced analytically as a two-asymptote log-uniform integral (|d| < 1e-3): G203 (b_inf 1.225, r_a 4.36) 0.4340; G209 E1 fit (b_inf 1.27, r_a 4.36) 0.4500; G206 FIT_A (b_inf 0.955, r_a 3.04) 0.4950

envelope.statement: the envelope region (3-5 R500) is 0.5-class (0.545-0.560); the window mean 0.434-0.438 is contaminated by the interior 2-3 bin (0.26-0.31)
envelope.verdict: 0.5 rule re-tested at the envelope bin: PASS (both estimators at or above 0.5)

ledger.number: recomputed window mean 0.447+-0.009 E1 / 0.417+-0.049 E2 reproduces committed 0.434+-0.015 / 0.438+-0.014 at |z|<=0.8; envelope bin 0.560+-0.015 / 0.545+-0.070 is 0.5-class

verdicts.V1: V1 THE PROFILE-WEIGHTED WINDOW MEAN: recomputed from the committed per-bin values with log-uniform weighting over [2,5] R500 (the committed beta_win_value convention, proven in C1): E1 0.447 +- 0.009; E2 0.417 +- 0.049 (per-draw bootstraps: E1 0.454 +- 0.012, E2 0.405 +- 0.052).  It reproduces the committed window means -- G203 0.434 +- 0.015 at z = +0.76 / -0.33, combined 0.438 +- 0.014 at z = +0.53 / -0.41 -- so the per-bin profile and the window-mean estimators describe the SAME anisotropy; no genuine estimator disagreement exists on the committed record.
verdicts.V2: V2 THE ENVELOPE-ONLY 0.5 TEST: at beta(3-5 R500) = 0.560 +- 0.015 (E1) / 0.545 +- 0.070 (E2), the 0.5 rule is NOT excluded: z = +4.1 / +0.6.  The envelope region is 0.5-class; the window mean 0.434-0.438 is diluted by the interior 2-3 bin (0.26-0.31); the -4.4 sigma exclusion does not transfer to the envelope bin.  The 0.5 rule re-tested AT the envelope bin: PASS (both estimators at or above 0.5).
verdicts.V3: V3 THE HONEST STATEMENT: the beta mean-vs-profile tension is an INTEGRAL/CATEGORY ARTIFACT, closed by the profile -- the window mean that excluded 0.5 at -4.4 sigma is the log-uniform average of the very per-bin profile that carries the 0.5-class envelope (recomputed 0.447/ 0.417 vs committed 0.434/0.438: |z| <= 0.8, C2), so there is NO estimator disagreement on the record.  The -4.4 sigma exclusion is real FOR THE WINDOW AVERAGE (interior 2-3 bin at 0.26-0.31 dilutes the rising profile; the PJ estimator's tight 0.015 error drives the combined z -- the 2D estimator alone, 0.495 +- 0.054, never excluded 0.5) but it was never in tension with the envelope claim, which lives at 3-5 R500 where the data measure 0.545-0.560 = 0.5-class (z = +4.1 / +0.6).  RESOLUTION: MOA #2 DISSOLVED.  The one genuinely live residue, kept on the record: the G170 rule AS REGISTERED at the WINDOW level (beta(2-5 R500) > 0.5 at >= 3 sigma) is not met (z = -4.4 combined) -- a real rule-level FAIL at the integration window, with the rule's envelope-level physical content confirmed -- and G209's g170_fixed shape remains the BIC winner with the rising two-regime map intact (REASSESSMENT section 2).

checks.name: C1 [convention identity] each committed window mean is reproduced by the exact log-uniform integral of its own committed two-asymptote form (|d| < 1e-3)
checks.reading: the 2-5 R500 window means are LOG-UNIFORM integrals -- the recomputation convention is exactly the committed convention, apples-to-apples.

checks.name: C2 [recomputation vs the committed window means -- THE CLOSURE TEST] the profile-weighted window mean from the committed per-bin values reproduces the committed 0.434-0.438 at |z| < 1.5 (both estimators, log-uniform)
checks.reading: the per-bin profile integrates back to the committed window numbers: the window mean IS the profile's log-uniform average, and the two estimators AGREE -- no estimator disagreement on the record.

checks.name: C3 [the 0.5 exclusion vs the recomputed window mean] the recomputed window mean itself also sits below 0.5 (a rising profile diluted by the interior 2-3 bin) -- the -4.4 sigma number is a property of the window AVERAGE, not an error
checks.reading: the recomputation does NOT rescue 0.5 at the window level (E1 still excludes it); the exclusion is REAL for the window mean, which is exactly why the window level was the wrong place to test the envelope claim.  The contradiction was a comparison category error, not a numerical one.

checks.name: C4 [envelope-only 0.5 test] at the 3-5 R500 bin the data are 0.5-class: neither estimator sits below 0.5 at |z| > 1.5
checks.reading: the envelope claim SURVIVES its own bin: 0.5 is not excluded at 3-5 R500 -- E1 sits above 0.5 at +4.1 sigma, E2 sits on 0.5 at +0.6 sigma.  The earlier 0.5-exclusion was a window-mean statement, not an envelope statement.
